alignments.note: Rule 20: the free genitive ἡμῶν supplies our and displaces the article's determiner, so the article realizes nothing. Rule 76's availability arm is not in question, ἡμῶν being spent on nothing else.
ἐλπίς → hope, the noun standing bare after rule 20 empties its article.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive our (rule 20).
Rule 53: the clause is verbless with an adjectival predicate, so the supplied copula is the adjective's helper; rule 17 heads it on the lexical stedfast rather than on is.
Rule 36: the English preposition governing the phrase realizes ὑπέρ.
Rule 43's test is the English: the ASV writes the complementizer that, so ὅτι is aligned to it in the ordinary way.
Comparative ὡς → as. Rule 82 is not in question, an expressed οὕτως carrying the correlative here.
κοινωνοί → partakers; ἐστε is expressed in this clause, so no copula is supplied for the predicate noun to carry.
Rule 9: the inflected verb takes its subject pronoun, headed on the verb are rather than on ye.
Rule 21: the genitive's case preposition of rides with the article, headed on the, and the noun stands alone.
Correlative οὕτως → so, the corpus rendering of the adverb.

Adverbial καί → also, decided on the English alone as rules 65 and 70 have it. Rule 82's correlative clause does not reach this καί: it speaks of a καί answering a comparative where no correlative adverb is expressed, and here οὕτως is expressed and takes so, so rule 2 keeps also its own unit.

Article with its case preposition riding along under rule 21, headed on *the*, exactly as the same verse's τῶν παθημάτων → *of the sufferings* takes *of the* on s013 — rule 24 requires the two comparative clauses to be analysed alike. The supplied *are ye* goes to the predicate noun rather than here: rule 68 gives a verbless clause's supplied subject and copula to the predicate, and no corpus unit puts a supplied subject pronoun on an article that does not itself realize a pronoun, while nine put subject and copula together on a predicate noun. Rule 62's παρά precedent does not carry, that being a preposition carrier and rule 67 warning that the analogy jumps carrier classes. Medium: GAL.2.20's τοῦ → *is in the* keeps a bare supplied copula on a determiner-carrying article, so the competing reading stays defensible.

Predicate noun of the elliptical second comparative clause, carrying the supplied subject and copula *are ye* under rule 68, discontinuously across s017's determiner under rule 15; head on *comfort* per rule 17. 2CO.5.13's θεῷ → *it is unto God* and ὑμῖν → *it is unto you* are the structural twins, and rule 92 records that a noun keeps the supplied copula even where an article beside it keeps its own English word. Medium with s017, the two readings dividing on which token carries *are ye*.

review_notes: Reviewed against the token table and returned with the unit structure, statuses and heads unchanged; only three notes were sharpened (s010, s016, s017) to name the rules a next reader would otherwise have to re-derive.
Every s### and t### id is partitioned exactly once: 18 source units covering s001-s018, and t001-t023 each claimed once.
s002 is the only unrepresented unit. ἡμῶν is a free genitive pronoun spent on nothing but the possessive, so rule 20 proper empties the article; rule 76's availability arm is not what decides it.

The two comparative halves are treated differently on purpose. The first expresses ἐστε and the predicate noun κοινωνοί, so nothing is supplied there; the second expresses neither subject nor verb, so rule 68 rather than rule 56 governs the supplied are ye — rule 56 wants a clause with no predicate at all, and τῆς παρακλήσεως is a predicate.

s017 is the one genuinely contested judgment and stays medium. The contract settles that the supplied words go to the predicate side but not which token of a genitive phrase carries them; rule 62 puts a supplied verb on the case-carrier, and rules 21 and 67 make the article that carrier here and hold the head on the.

Rule 82 was checked and does not apply: it gives the correlative so to a καί answering a comparative adverb that has only as, whereas οὕτως is expressed in this verse and takes so itself, leaving καί its own also.
